PullRequest.Title: base: remove unused traceable time API shim
PullRequest.Body:
Removes the deprecated traceableTimeApi re-export shim after confirming there are no remaining repository references. Updates the virtual scheduling migration note and removes the obsolete stack-frame filter entry. The active timeTravelScheduler compatibility shim is unchanged because it still has callers.

Validation:
- npm run eslint -- src/vs/base/test/common/virtualScheduling/index.ts src/vs/base/test/common/executionGraph.ts — passed.
- git diff --check — passed.
- npm run compile-client — blocked before compilation: package.json declares Copilot runtime 1.0.99-1, but @github/copilot-sdk bundles 1.0.99-0.
- .\scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --run src/vs/base/test/common/executionGraph.test.ts — blocked because generated out/vs/platform/protocol/electron-main/remoteResourceProtocol.js is missing.

No related issue was provided.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compile and load the base test virtual-scheduling utilities after removing the deprecated traceableTimeApi re-export module
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository search found no imports or references to traceableTimeApi.ts/.js, so normal test execution has no module-load dependency on the deleted shim. A clean source build may discover one fewer source file; active callers already import virtualScheduling/index.js directly. No newly added work blocks startup, rendering, or tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build tooling discovers and, on relevant clean builds, reads/transpiles repository TypeScript sources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fewer source-file read/transpile operation; there are zero repository import resolutions targeting this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deprecated re-export file existed and could be included by source discovery, although no repository caller imported it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff removes rather than adds this build input, so it cannot increase build critical-path I/O.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One deleted 19-line re-export file; effective runtime caller cardinality is zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Module discovery/transpilation concurrency is owned by the existing build tooling; the diff adds no tasks, queue, limiter, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold builds can omit the deleted source file; warm/incremental builds have no active import edge to resolve. No application cache key, miss path, coalescing, or negative cache is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete changed-file inventory and repository-wide searches establish that the shim has no active callers and that the replacement exports remain in virtualScheduling/index.ts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact build-tool source inclusion is configuration-dependent, but that uncertainty only affects whether the tiny removed cost existed; there is no mechanism for added cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The change removes dead source and leaves all active implementation exports unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render virtual-time execution histories for component fixtures and inline-completion tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: buildHistoryFromTasks synchronously extracts caller frames once per traced task, and renderSwimlanes runs afterward. Component fixtures invoke this diagnostic path only on virtual-time failures or when outputTimeTrace is explicitly requested; inline-completion tests invoke it only when logTimeTrace is enabled. It is not on the normal editor/product rendering path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The component fixture processor caps execution at 200 events per render. Frame extraction scans each task's stack lines until five accepted frames; inline test histories scale with their recorded timer-event count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: History construction and rendering are synchronous and serialized after timer processing. The fixture's render and virtual-time processor may run through an existing Promise.all beforehand, but the diff does not change that concurrency or create aggregate work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache on this diagnostic path before or after the diff. Each requested history is constructed once from the current run; no cache miss, invalidation, coalescing, or retry behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed regular expression remains one test per stack line and is strictly simpler after removing an obsolete alternation; direct caller tracing establishes bounded and diagnostic-only execution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Historical or externally fabricated stack strings could still contain the deleted filename, but repository search found none; even then output remains capped at five detail frames per task.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Current stack traces cannot originate from the deleted module, and the regex edit neither increases regex count nor moves history processing onto a hotter path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use the active virtualScheduling barrel and retained timeTravelScheduler compatibility shim in tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Callers import implementation symbols from virtualScheduling/index.js, while remaining legacy callers can still resolve timeTravelScheduler.ts. The diff changes only a migration comment in the active barrel and does not alter export initialization or runtime scheduling.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales with existing test imports and scheduled events, but the exported module graph and scheduler implementation are unchanged for every active caller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: VirtualClock and VirtualTimeProcessor retain their existing scheduling and processing semantics; no new parallel work, serialization point, queue, or limiter is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ES module caching behavior for active imports is unchanged. The removed module had zero repository consumers, so neither cold nor warm module resolution gains an extra load.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for repository scenarios because all references were searched and the active barrel exports were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Out-of-repository consumers of an internal test path are not visible, but removal would be compatibility behavior rather than a demonstrated performance mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The active implementation and retained compatibility path perform exactly the same scheduling work as before.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all relevant callers. The PR deletes an unreferenced re-export shim, updates its migration comment, and removes the obsolete filename from a bounded test-diagnostic stack filter. No changed path adds repeated work, allocation, I/O, retention, fan-out, or concurrency, and no concrete shipped performance regression fix requiring blame was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
